Right page: running head at top; one main text column with a line-number column (2449, 2454, 2459 year marks) set beside it; marginal note at right beside the first paragraph lines; full text column below the head area. main_text.p: Deos fructibus colere, animalia non laedere, fancivit. Amphictyon ipse Deucalionis F. Concilii (in quo Graecia secundum communes leges, in Delphici Apollinis adyto, initio veris & autumni quotannis, per suos Pylagoras judicabat, & cujus sententiae raro irritae transmittebantur,) auctor, qui primus vinum miscuit, utque dilutum ad satietatem addito Jovis Servatoris nomine bibere tur, constituit. Erychthonius Vulcani & Minervae F. qui Amphictyonem ejecit, tribubus quatuor nomina immutavit, & primus argentum vel invenit, vel Athenas attulit, vel inscripsit.

In ARCADIA novum inchoasse videtur regnum Pelasgus, qui tunicas e suillis coriis confuere, glandibus vesci, domos exstruere eos docuit. Successere ipsi Lycaon, qui primus obtide, quem a Molossis acceperat, Jovi immolato, inducias viPausan in Arcad.olavit: Nictymus, & Arcas, qui primus panem facere docuit, & vestium texturam, totumque lanificium, quod ab Adrifta dedicerat, monstravit. Ab eo ad Agapenorem, qui Trojano bello interfuit, varia fortuna regnatum est. Licurgi, IX. Re gis filius, erat Anceus, qui imprecatione servorum duriter habitorum & vitam & vineam amisit.

In AETOLIA, quæ ad sinum Corinthiacum, qua is mari Jonio proximior, administravit regnum Oenèus. Quid ibidem ad ultima usque tempora fit actum, non traditur. Habuit duos filios, quorum major Meleager, Herculis per Dejaniram sororem affinis, Hylli patruus, aprum Caledonium peremit; minor natu ex matre Aetolici generis Tydeus, acceptâ uxore Deiphile Adrasti Regis F. Diomedem progenuit.

page.notes: Left page is mostly cut off; only fragments of the left column are visible and are not transcribed. Marginal year numbers 2449, 2454, 2459 are printed beside the text and are not part of the running text. Some letters in the right column are uncertain. The leftmost strip shows fragments of a facing page's text, cut off; not transcribed. The word "imprecatione" and "Oenèus" read as printed. Signature "D 2" and catchword "In" are at the foot of the page.
